newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BNZ sees growth in non-banking areas.
newsitem.headline: BNZ sees growth in non-banking areas.

text.p: The National Australia Bank owned Bank of New Zealand said on Thursday its strongest growth area has been in funds management and it sees further strong growth there.
Managing director Gordon Wheaton, speaking at a briefing on the bank's NZ$194 million half year operating profit, said the bank's strategy was to become a provider of total financial solutions.
Head of the bank's financial services group, David Jones, said the sector was the fastest growing in the bank.
Unit trust business grew by 10.4 percent, superannuation by 7.3 percent and life insurance by 8.4 percent in the half year.
Jones said an IPAC survey showed BNZ as the fastest growth fund manager and its balanced fund as the top performer across all periods.
Overall, the bank was now the fifth largest funds manager in New Zealand with NZ$1.1 billion under management.
"Our goal is to be number one," Jones said.
Wheaton noted life companies were encroaching into traditional banking areas, with the example of the AMP considering an application for a banking licence.
"We are also looking towards moving into their traditional markets," Wheaton said.
